title: ML111 Test 1 Mock Exam - Safety, Dilutions, Measurement & QA
instructions: Weighted like the real test: Safety 35-40%, Dilutions 25-30%, Math/Systems of Measurement & Statistics 20-25%, QA & QSEs 5-10%. Answer each question, check your result, read the explanation, then move on. Goal: 100%.

questions.question: Which class of hazard includes repetitive stress injuries from microscopes and computer workstations?
questions.explanation: Ergonomic hazards = noise, standing, bending, repetitive stress injuries, microscopes and computer workstations.

questions.question: Bacteria, viruses, rickettsiae, fungi and parasites belong to which hazard class?
questions.explanation: Biological hazards cause infections from these 5 organisms. Memory hook: BVRFP - 'Bad Viruses Really Fear Penicillin'.

questions.question: Headaches, loss of appetite and insomnia are symptoms of which hazard class?
questions.explanation: Psychosocial hazards (stress, abuse, harassment) show physical symptoms like headaches, insomnia and loss of appetite, plus behavioural and mental/emotional symptoms.

questions.question: The correct ORDER of effectiveness of control measures is:
questions.explanation: Engineering (fix the hazard at the source, like a fume hood) is most effective. PPE is the LAST line of defence - like a seatbelt, not the brakes.

questions.question: Which of these is an ENGINEERING control?
questions.explanation: Engineering controls remove the hazard at the source: fume hoods, biosafety cabinets, guards, substitution of less toxic substances. Training and orientation are administrative; gloves are personal.

questions.question: Scheduling workers to avoid overexposure is which type of control?
questions.explanation: Administrative controls = rules and schedules: orientation, safe work procedures, training, scheduling, inspections, emergency plans.

questions.question: TLV stands for - and means:
options: Total Limit Value - the legal fine
Threshold Limit Value - the highest level you can be exposed to without ill effects
Tested Laboratory Value - lowest detectable level
questions.explanation: TLV = Threshold Limit Value = the HIGHEST level of exposure without ill effects. Standards come from the provincial government responsible for OHS.

questions.question: Due diligence means:
options: Blaming the employee after an accident
Doing everything reasonable to protect worker health and safety
questions.explanation: Due diligence = take all reasonable precautions to prevent injuries. It is the legal responsibility of the EMPLOYER and requires training, record keeping, enforcement and clear policies.

questions.question: Bill C-45 (Canada Criminal Code) means failure to direct work safely can lead to:
questions.explanation: Bill C-45 creates a legal duty for anyone directing work to take reasonable steps for safety. Failure = CRIMINAL NEGLIGENCE.

questions.question: The three components of WHMIS 2015 are:
options: SDS, labels/classifications, employee education and training
questions.explanation: WHMIS 2015 = (1) Safety Data Sheet (SDS, formerly MSDS), (2) Labels and classifications, (3) Employee education and training.

questions.question: A supplier label must be written in:
questions.explanation: Supplier labels must be bilingual (French AND English) and include: product identifier, supplier, pictogram, signal word, hazard statements and precautionary statements.

questions.question: A workplace label is REQUIRED when:
options: A product is decanted into another container
The supplier label is lost or illegible
A hazardous product is produced at the workplace and used there
questions.explanation: All three situations require a workplace label. Exception: if used IMMEDIATELY or used only by the person who decanted it during that shift - then only the product identifier is needed.

questions.question: A hazardous product poured into a beaker for IMMEDIATE use must be labelled with:
questions.explanation: Immediate use or same-person same-shift use = only the product identifier is required. This is a classic trap question.

questions.question: Transport of Dangerous Goods (TDG) for HIGHWAYS is controlled by which level of government?
questions.explanation: Provincial handles TDG for highways. Federal handles TDG for RAIL AND SEAWAY. Municipal handles fire and building codes. H&S legislation is PRIMARILY provincial.

questions.question: A hazard is best defined as:
options: The chance an injury will occur
Anything with the potential to cause injury or illness
questions.explanation: Hazard = potential to cause harm. Risk = the CHANCE it actually happens. Not all hazards are risks.

questions.question: The FIRST step of a job hazard assessment is to:
options: List the critical/major steps of the job
questions.explanation: Order: (1) list 5-10 major steps, (2) identify equipment/procedures, (3) identify hazards at each step (think worst case), (4) implement controls, (5) verify effectiveness.

questions.question: A risk assessment rates which three factors from 1 to 4?
questions.explanation: Risk = Probability x Severity x Frequency of exposure, each rated 1-4, then classified.

questions.question: A fire in a bin of solvent-soaked rags is which class?
questions.explanation: Class B = liquid fuels (solvents, oil, gasoline). A = ordinary combustibles (wood, paper), C = electrical, D = combustible metals, K = cooking oils/fats.

questions.question: Why can flames reignite after using a CO2 extinguisher?
questions.explanation: CO2 smothers the fire but the gas blows away fast, so hot material can catch fire again. CO2 is also ineffective on Class A fires.

questions.question: The eyewash and safety shower must provide water flow for ___ and be reachable within ___:
questions.explanation: 15 minutes of flow ('you have TIME to SEE again') and reachable within 10 seconds. Memorize both numbers.

questions.question: For a LARGE chemical spill, your FIRST action is to:
options: Wipe it up with paper towel
questions.explanation: Large spill = evacuate immediately, then call 922 from a safe location and give responders the SDS. Small spills with no odours can be handled with the spill kit.

questions.question: Biohazardous waste is rendered harmless by:
questions.explanation: Biohazardous waste (blood, bodily fluids, contaminated materials) is stored separately and autoclaved or chemically treated.

questions.question: In the college lab, security is reached by dialing:
questions.explanation: Dial 922 from any college phone, 24 hours a day. 475-6624 is Health & Safety for spill disposal arrangements.

questions.question: A 1:10 RATIO of sample to diluent is actually which dilution?
questions.explanation: THE #1 mark-loser. 1:10 ratio = 1 part sample + 10 parts diluent = 11 total parts = a 1/11 DILUTION. A 1/10 dilution means 1 sample + 9 diluent.

questions.question: Dilution is calculated as:
questions.explanation: Dilution = sample volume divided by TOTAL volume. The bottom number always includes the sample itself.

questions.question: You mix 20 mcL of sample with 80 mcL of diluent. The dilution is:
questions.explanation: Total = 20 + 80 = 100 mcL. 20/100 = 1/5 dilution.

questions.question: A 1/5 dilution of serum gives a creatinine result of 4.5 mg/dL. The actual concentration in the original sample is:
questions.explanation: Diluted result x dilution factor = original. Factor = reciprocal of 1/5 = 5. So 4.5 x 5 = 22.5 mg/dL.

questions.question: A 1/1000 final dilution made by serial dilution using equal steps would be:
questions.explanation: Serial dilution: multiply the fractions. 1/10 x 1/10 x 1/10 = 1/1000. Same dilution in each tube.

questions.question: In a serial 10-fold dilution, tube 3 has a dilution of:
In a serial DOUBLING dilution, tube 4 has a dilution of:
questions.explanation: Doubling: tube x = 1/(2^x). Tube 4 = 1/16. (Tube 1 = 1/2, tube 2 = 1/4, tube 3 = 1/8, tube 4 = 1/16.) Used in serology for antibody strength.

questions.question: In a TUBE dilution series, each tube has:
questions.explanation: Tube dilution series = DIFFERENT dilution per tube. Each tube's concentration = previous tube's concentration divided by that tube's dilution factor.

questions.question: A 1650 mg/dL sample goes through tubes diluted 1/5 then 1/2. The concentration in tube 2 is:
A titer is:
options: The first tube with a reaction
The inverse of the dilution where the LAST measurable reaction occurred
questions.explanation: Titer = inverse of the last positive dilution in an antigen-antibody test. If the last positive is 1/640, the titer is 640.

questions.question: Serial dilutions of serum show positive reactions up to 1/320 but not at 1/640. The titer is:
questions.explanation: Last measurable reaction = 1/320, so the titer = 320 (the inverse). A LOW titer of a protective antibody may mean NO immunity.

questions.question: In microbiology, antibiotics are diluted to determine the:
questions.explanation: Why we dilute: chemistry = result outside the instrument's linear range; microbiology = MIC; immunology = titers.

questions.question: To make a 1/4 dilution with a total volume of 100 mcL, you need:
questions.explanation: Ratio and proportion: 1/4 = X/100, so X = 25 mcL sample. Diluent = 100 - 25 = 75 mcL.

questions.question: Which is an example of a SEMIQUANTITATIVE measurement?
questions.explanation: Quantitative = precise number. Qualitative = yes/no. Semiquantitative = an ESTIMATE of amount, like dipstick grades.

questions.question: The SI system is based on how many basic units?
questions.explanation: SI has SEVEN units: meter, kilogram, mole, second, ampere, kelvin, candela. SI is the revised metric system (1960, revised 1971) replacing older metric in labs.

questions.question: Convert 12 mL to mcL using the exponent method.
questions.explanation: milli = 10^-3, micro = 10^-6, difference = 3 places to the right: 12 mL = 12,000 mcL.

questions.question: Convert 98.6 F to Celsius.
questions.explanation: C = (F - 32) x 5/9 = (98.6 - 32) x 5/9 = 66.6 x 5/9 = 37 C. Normal body temperature.

questions.question: MCV (mean cell volume) is reported in which unit?
questions.explanation: MCV uses femtoliters (10^-15). Know the prefix ladder: kilo 10^3 down to femto 10^-15.

questions.question: Results: 4, 7, 7, 9, 12. The mean, median and mode are:
questions.explanation: Mean = 39/5 = 7.8. Median = middle number = 7. Mode = most frequent = 7. In a Gaussian distribution all three would be equal.

questions.question: Accuracy and precision are best described as:
options: Accuracy = repeatability, precision = closeness to true value
Accuracy = closeness to the true value, precision = same result on repeated analysis
questions.explanation: Bullseye picture: accuracy = hitting the center (true value); precision = tight grouping (repeatable). We want BOTH.

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of results fall within +/- 2 SD of the mean in a normal distribution?
questions.explanation: Memorize: +/-1 SD = 68.2%, +/-2 SD = 95.5%, +/-3 SD = 99.7%. Reference ranges are usually set at mean +/- 2 SD (95% of healthy people).

questions.question: Coefficient of variation (CV) is calculated as:
questions.explanation: CV = (SD / mean) x 100. It expresses SD as a percentage so you can compare precision between different tests. LOWER CV = better precision.

questions.question: If QC is NOT in control, patient results are:
questions.explanation: QC in control = results CAN be reported. QC out of control = results are NOT released until the problem is fixed.

questions.question: Analytical specificity is the ability to:
options: Detect the presence of the target molecule
Distinguish the target from other molecules (true negative)
questions.explanation: Sensitivity = detecting the target's presence (true positive). Specificity = distinguishing the target from other molecules (true negative).

questions.question: QMP-LS is funded by:
options: The Ministry of Health & Long Term Care
questions.explanation: QMP-LS oversees licensed Ontario labs and is funded by the MOHLTC. It is responsible for IQMH (formerly OLA) and EQA.

questions.question: QC vs QA: which statement is correct?
options: QA is a component of QC
QC is a component of QA
questions.explanation: QA is the big umbrella (all policies to assure quality patient care). QC is one component under it - the specific checks employees perform.

questions.question: Routine Practices are also known as standard or universal precautions.
questions.explanation: Routine Practices = standard/universal precautions - treat every specimen as potentially infectious.

questions.question: It is acceptable to pipette by mouth if you are careful and the solution is not toxic.
questions.explanation: NEVER pipette by mouth. No exceptions. Always use a bulb or pipette aid.

questions.question: During a fire evacuation you should close but NOT lock doors, and use the stairs.
questions.explanation: Close doors (do not lock), exit calmly by the stairs - never the elevator - and call 922.

questions.question: An injured person should always be moved immediately to a comfortable location.
questions.explanation: Do NOT move an injured person unless required for safety. Make them comfortable where they are and call 922.

questions.question: A 1:4 ratio of sample to diluent is the same as a 1/4 dilution.
questions.explanation: 1:4 ratio = 1 sample + 4 diluent = 5 total parts = a 1/5 dilution. Ratios and dilutions are NOT the same.

questions.question: In a serial dilution, the final dilution is found by ADDING the individual dilutions.
questions.explanation: You MULTIPLY them: 1/10 x 1/10 x 1/10 = 1/1000.

questions.question: A smaller variance indicates a MORE precise set of results.
questions.explanation: Variance shows how close together the numbers are. Smaller variance = tighter grouping = more precise.

questions.question: Military (24-hour) time is used in hospitals to reduce documentation and medication errors.
questions.explanation: Hospitals operate 24/7, and the 24-hour clock removes AM/PM confusion, reducing errors.

questions.question: Defective equipment should be clearly marked and removed from service.
questions.explanation: Equipment QSE: defective equipment is marked and REMOVED; new equipment is VALIDATED before use.

questions.question: For stock rotation, new reagents go to the BACK and older stock moves to the FRONT.
questions.explanation: First in, first out. Older stock gets used first so nothing expires - critically important for lot number tracking.

questions.question: Match each fire class to what is burning.

pairs.right: Ordinary combustibles (wood, paper, cloth)
Liquid fuels (solvents, oil, gasoline)
Electrical equipment (fuse boxes, motors)
Cooking media (oils, lards, fats)

questions.explanation: Do not forget Class D = combustible metals (sodium, potassium). Water extinguishers are dangerous around lab equipment and some chemicals.

questions.question: Match each level of government to its safety responsibility.

pairs.right: OH&S Act and TDG for highways
Canada Labour Code, TDG rail and seaway, Bill C-45
Fire codes and building codes
Routine Practices and its own procedures

questions.explanation: H&S legislation is PRIMARILY provincial, but know what federal and municipal each own.

questions.question: Match each statistics term to its meaning.

pairs.right: Sum of values divided by n
The central number when values are in order
The most frequently occurring value
Mean, median and mode are all equal

questions.explanation: In a normal (Gaussian) bell curve all three measures sit at the same central point.

questions.question: Match each dilution type to its description.

pairs.right: Same dilution in each tube of the series
Every tube is 1/2 of the one before (used in serology)
Every tube is 1/10 of the one before
A different dilution in each tube

questions.explanation: Serial = same step repeated. Fold tells you the step size (doubling = 1/2, 10-fold = 1/10). Tube series = different each tube.

questions.question: Match each quality term to its definition.

pairs.right: Specific, objective, well-defined, measurable monitors
System lab management must establish, document, implement and maintain
Let the lab track products to pinpoint problems
Capturing nonconforming events and finding root causes

questions.explanation: These come from the QA and 12 QSEs section - small part of the test but easy marks.
